title: Cryptool vs Blockpit
content_html:
Blockpit is a crypto tax and accounting platform built for investors and businesses that need compliant reporting across jurisdictions. Cryptool.io is an investment operating system that combines portfolio tracking with fund administration, syndicate management and capital raising. Blockpit is the better choice when tax reporting is the primary need. Cryptool.io is the better choice when managing investments, allocations and investor positions across multiple wallets and deals.

What Blockpit is good at

Blockpit specializes in crypto tax reporting and accounting. The platform connects to wallets and exchanges, categorizes transactions, and generates tax reports for multiple jurisdictions including Austria, Germany, Switzerland, the UK and the US. This is their core focus and they do it well.

Blockpit handles DeFi transactions, staking rewards, airdrops and NFT trades. The platform applies local tax rules automatically and produces reports that accountants and tax authorities accept. For investors who need compliant tax documentation at year end, Blockpit is a genuine specialist.

The platform also offers portfolio tracking as part of the tax workflow, showing current holdings and historical performance. Businesses get accounting features including balance sheet preparation and audit trails.

What Cryptool.io does differently

Cryptool.io is built for the investment operations side. Portfolio tracking sits alongside fund administration, syndicate management and capital raising in one non-custodial platform.

The portfolio module tracks holdings across all chains and all wallet providers. Add wallets from MetaMask, Ledger, Trust Wallet or any other provider and balances update automatically. On-chain modules run on EVM chains and MultiversX, with more coming.

Fund administration means running the books, allocations and investor positions of a fund or syndicate from one system. Track member commitments, calculate allocations, set vesting schedules and generate investor reports without spreadsheets. The [multi-chain portfolio tracker with fund admin](/blog/multi-chain-portfolio-tracker-with-fund-admin) approach means position data and member allocations live in the same place.

Capital raising runs end to end on the platform. Set up a pool, define tiers, collect commitments and distribute tokens according to vesting schedules you configure at deal creation. Identity verification, document management and automated distribution are included. Groups running [a crypto syndicate](/blog/how-to-run-a-crypto-syndicate) use this to manage member allocations and distributions without manual tracking.

The OTC marketplace lets participants negotiate and settle over-the-counter trades for allocations, including unvested positions. [OTC desk software for crypto](/blog/otc-desk-software-for-crypto) that operates non-custodially means settlement happens between counterparties, not through a custodian.

Cryptool.io also handles deal flow, sourcing and stage tracking for venture capital workflows, plus an investor CRM for tracking commitments and communications.

Which one should you pick

Pick Blockpit when tax compliance is the priority. If you need reports for your accountant, documentation for tax authorities, or compliant accounting for a business, Blockpit is built for that and does it well. The platform supports multiple jurisdictions and handles complex transaction types including DeFi and staking.

Pick Cryptool.io when investment operations are the priority. If you run a fund, manage a syndicate, operate a launchpad or need to track allocations and investor positions alongside your portfolio, Cryptool.io handles those workflows in one place. The platform is non-custodial and supports all chains and wallet providers for portfolio tracking.

Pick both if you need tax reporting and investment operations. Blockpit can handle the tax side while Cryptool.io manages the operational side. The two platforms serve different parts of the workflow.

Avoid Cryptool.io if tax reporting is your only need. The platform does not generate tax forms or apply jurisdiction-specific rules, and building that workflow elsewhere makes more sense.

Avoid Blockpit if fund administration, syndicate management or capital raising are the primary needs. The platform is not built for those workflows and you would need separate tools to handle them.

FAQ

What is the difference between cryptool vs blockpit?

Blockpit is a crypto tax and accounting platform that generates compliant reports for multiple jurisdictions. Cryptool.io is an investment operating system that combines portfolio tracking with fund administration, syndicate management and capital raising. Blockpit focuses on tax compliance. Cryptool.io focuses on investment operations.

Does Blockpit handle fund administration?

No. Blockpit is built for tax reporting and accounting, not fund administration. Managing member allocations, investor positions and capital raising requires a separate platform. Cryptool.io handles fund administration alongside portfolio tracking in one system.

Does Cryptool.io generate tax reports?

No. Cryptool.io tracks portfolio positions and manages investment operations, but does not generate tax forms or apply jurisdiction-specific tax rules. Investors who need compliant tax documentation should use a specialist platform like Blockpit or Koinly.

Can I use both platforms together?

Yes. Blockpit can handle tax reporting while Cryptool.io manages investment operations. The two platforms serve different parts of the workflow and do not overlap. You would track portfolio and fund operations on Cryptool.io and export transaction data to Blockpit for tax reporting.

Which platform supports more chains?

Both platforms support multi-chain portfolio tracking. Cryptool.io supports all chains and all wallet providers for portfolio tracking, with on-chain modules running on EVM chains and MultiversX. Blockpit supports the major chains and exchanges for transaction import and tax calculation. Chain coverage is not the deciding factor between them.

Is either platform custodial?

No. Both Blockpit and Cryptool.io are non-custodial. Wallet connections are read-only and neither platform holds private keys or signing authority. Your funds stay in your own wallets.
